runs.answer: I recommend **1 doublet at 2,500 m, heat pump top-up and a gas boiler (3 units), electric chillers, sized so that any one unit can be out (N-1): boiler and chillers in equal units** (A1 · 1D-HP-EC-N1-FC), the best overall: a reliable plan (any one unit can be out and every day is still met) and, of those, the cheapest when CO₂ counts at 137 €/t (the long-term price). It meets heat at 100 °C and cold at 20 °C every day of 2027 for 66.6 €/MWh of heat and cold together (heat 75.7 €/MWh, cold 23.5 €/MWh), with 48.8% less CO₂ than gas boilers and electric chillers, and passes all 15 checks. Its heat: the geothermal exchanger 37.4%, the heat pump 19.7%, the gas boiler 42.9% (it burns the produced gas first and buys 39.3 GWh of gas a year).

runs.message: What happens to the recommended design if the reservoir is 10 C colder and the boiler is 20 MW?
runs.answer: With reservoir -10 K, boiler size 20 MW, 1D-HP-EC-N1-FC with its present sizes covers 99.8% of the heat and 100% of the cold. Heat and cold cost 74.2 €/MWh (was 66.6); the CO₂ saving against gas is 31.6% (was 48.8%). The heat exchanger gives 19.4% of the heat (was 37.4%), the heat pump 22% (was 19.7%) and the boiler 58.5% (was 42.9%). The brine goes back at 45.7 °C at the coldest (was 52.1 °C). With these sizes it breaks a cap: Heat short of 100 °C supply on 7 day(s): worst 2.90 MW on 28 Jan (demand 30.00 MW). Against gas under the change (gas boilers and chillers at the same prices): NPV 10.7 M€ (was 26.1 M€), paying back in year 16. Searching again under the change picks 1D-HP-EC-N1-FC-PV2.9 at 72.8 €/MWh instead of 1D-HP-EC-N1-FC: 1 doublet at 2,500 m, heat pump top-up and a gas boiler (3 units), electric chillers, sized so that any one unit can be out (N-1): boiler and chillers in equal units.

runs.message: What happens to the design if we lower the heating return temperature to 50 °C?
runs.answer: With heating return temperature 50 °C, 1D-HP-EC-N1-FC with its present sizes covers 100% of the heat and 100% of the cold. Heat and cold cost 62.8 €/MWh (was 66.6); the CO₂ saving against gas is 59.7% (was 48.8%). The heat exchanger gives 50.8% of the heat (was 37.4%), the heat pump 18.5% (was 19.7%) and the boiler 30.7% (was 42.9%). The brine goes back at 42.6 °C at the coldest (was 52.1 °C). Against gas under the change (gas boilers and chillers at the same prices): NPV 33.7 M€ (was 26.1 M€), paying back in year 10. Searching again under the change picks 1D-HP-EC-N1-FC-PV1.7 at 60.1 €/MWh instead of 1D-HP-EC-N1-FC: 1 doublet at 2,500 m, heat pump top-up and a gas boiler (3 units), electric chillers, sized so that any one unit can be out (N-1): boiler and chillers in equal units.
